policy: Original morphological descriptions, revision-derived characters, secondary accounts and dated national/global conservation assessments remain separately typed; no family-level filler or inferred field occurrence.

facts.label: Comparative skull
facts.text: The skull has a long, downward-sloping facial region in front of the canines, distinguishing examined Mindoro specimens from Sus philippensis.
facts.source: IUCN SSC Wild Pig Specialist Group, Oliver's Warty Pig detailed account
facts.sourceLocation: Descriptive notes, based on three male skulls
facts.studyScope: Skull comparison only; the source warns that external field appearance and hybrid ancestry remain uncertain.

facts.label: Beard and adult coat
facts.text: Adult Palawan bearded pigs have long whitish cheek-and-jowl hair and a pale mane contrasting with darker facial hair; young animals lack the adult beard.
facts.source: IUCN SSC Wild Pig Specialist Group, Palawan Bearded Pig detailed account
facts.studyScope: Adult features vary by age. Species-level identification also needs context and comparison.

facts.label: Tail and body
facts.text: The long, heavily furred tail and dense brown-to-black body coat with paler flanks are documented for the Luzon bushy-tailed cloud rat.
facts.source: University of Michigan Animal Diversity Web, Crateromys schadenbergi account
facts.studyScope: Source is a secondary compilation; no specimen verification or molecular key.

facts.label: Dorsal marks in revised taxonomy
facts.text: Published taxonomic revision distinguishes this monitor by five to eight transverse rows of yellow ocelli on a dark back, a mostly dark head with yellow markings, and a temporal stripe.
facts.source: Welton et al. (2014), Varanus samarensis taxonomic diagnosis on Zenodo
facts.sourceLocation: Diagnosis, drawing on Koch et al. (2010)
facts.studyScope: Combined traits from sampled specimens; individual markings may vary and are not site occurrence evidence.

facts.label: Scalation in diagnosis
facts.text: The taxonomic diagnosis records 115–145 scales around the midbody and 158–180 ventral scale rows; juveniles can show four to six transverse rows of pale dorsal spots.
facts.source: The Reptile Database, Varanus marmoratus diagnosis summarizing taxonomic work
facts.studyScope: Microscopic scale-count characters from comparative specimens; counts are not a simple photo-based key.

facts.label: Unspotted adult deer
facts.text: Adults are usually uniform dark-brown without a spotted coat; males bear relatively short, slender, three-tined antlers, with regional variation.
facts.source: Handbook of the Mammals of the World, Rusa marianna account, Plazi transcription
facts.studyScope: Adult deer only; juveniles and local populations vary. Do not infer sex from coat color.

facts.label: Palawan forest mosaic
facts.text: Documented habitats include lowland and middle-elevation rainforest, dry open woodland, limestone forest, mangrove forest and some cultivated landscapes.
facts.source: IUCN SSC Wild Pig Specialist Group, Palawan Bearded Pig
facts.studyScope: Regional species habitat account, not confirmed presence at a field station.

facts.label: Montane forest habitats
facts.text: A secondary mammal account reports pine and mossy forests in northern Luzon, with described records around 2,000–2,500 m elevation.
facts.source: University of Michigan Animal Diversity Web, Crateromys schadenbergi
facts.studyScope: Reported account range, not a hard ecological elevation limit.

facts.label: Nocturnal climbing
facts.text: The species account describes tree use and night activity, with daytime shelter in tree hollows or spaces near roots.
facts.source: University of Michigan Animal Diversity Web, Crateromys schadenbergi
facts.studyScope: Secondary natural-history summary, not quantified telemetry.

facts.label: Recorded forest use
facts.text: The published deer monograph describes the Philippine brown deer in forest environments; a local 2025 study documents cultural and hunting context in Mindanao.
facts.source: Handbook of the Mammals of the World, Rusa marianna account, Plazi transcription
facts.studyScope: Account applies to the species and not to a validated local survey site.

facts.label: Tawi-Tawi lowland forest
facts.text: The 2021 global assessment identifies tropical moist lowland forest as suitable habitat and treats the species' current persistence as uncertain.
facts.source: BirdLife International (2021), IUCN Gallicolumba menagei global assessment
facts.studyScope: Historical species-level habitat; no confirmed sightings since 1891 are established by this assessment.

facts.label: IUCN global status, 2021
facts.text: The June 2021 global assessment lists Sulu Bleeding-heart as Critically Endangered under criterion D, with a very small inferred remaining population.
facts.source: BirdLife International (2021), IUCN Gallicolumba menagei
facts.studyScope: Dated global status; not proof of extant birds and not Philippine DENR legal classification.

facts.label: Forest habitats
facts.text: The 2021 global assessment identifies forest and some human-modified terrestrial habitats, with a listed elevational upper limit near 900 m.
facts.source: BirdLife International (2021), IUCN Anthracoceros marchei
facts.studyScope: Global range account; does not establish site-level presence.

facts.label: IUCN global status, 2021
facts.text: BirdLife assessed the Palawan Hornbill as Vulnerable in July 2021 with a decreasing population trend; logging, trapping and mining feature among listed threats.
facts.source: BirdLife International (2021), IUCN Anthracoceros marchei
facts.studyScope: Global dated category and threat list, not Philippine national assessment.

facts.label: IUCN global status, 2021
facts.text: BirdLife's 2021 global assessment lists the Negros Bleeding-heart as Critically Endangered (C2a(i)), citing forest loss and trapping pressure.
facts.source: BirdLife International, Negros Bleeding-heart IUCN 2021, BirdLife DataZone
facts.studyScope: Global dated status; no independent site abundance estimate is inferred.

facts.label: IUCN global status, 2023
facts.text: BirdLife's 2023 global assessment lists Mindanao Bleeding-heart as Vulnerable, identifying ongoing forest clearance and a decreasing population trend.
facts.source: BirdLife International, Mindanao Bleeding-heart, BirdLife DataZone
facts.studyScope: Global assessment distinct from DENR national status. Current population size remains unknown.

facts.label: Freshwater habitats
facts.text: Philippine crocodiles inhabit freshwater rivers, ponds and marshes; contemporary conservation sites include both riverine and wetland settings.
facts.source: Smithsonian National Zoo, Philippine crocodile species account
facts.studyScope: General habitat range, not a spatial distribution prediction.

facts.label: Parental nest guarding
facts.text: Smithsonian's species account describes females making mound or hole nests and both sexes guarding the nest; recorded clutches comprise seven to thirty eggs.
facts.source: Smithsonian National Zoo, Philippine crocodile species account
facts.studyScope: Summary of documented behaviour, not site-specific nest monitoring.

facts.label: DENR national status, 2019
facts.text: DENR-PENRO Cotabato reports the Philippine crocodile as Critically Endangered under DENR Administrative Order 2019-09 in a June 2025 national conservation notice.
facts.source: DENR-PENRO Cotabato (9 June 2025), Philippine crocodile rescue
facts.sourceLocation: DENR DAO 2019-09 citation in agency announcement
facts.studyScope: Philippine national status, not IUCN assessment; dated notice does not establish global listing.

facts.label: IUCN global status, assessed 2016
facts.text: The 2016 global IUCN assessment (published 2017) lists Palawan Bearded Pig as Near Threatened, with a declining population trend.
facts.source: Meijaard & Widmann (2017), IUCN Sus ahoenobarbus assessment
facts.studyScope: Dated global category. The specialist-group page contains conflicting historical text and is not used for the assessment label.
